newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras unveils plan to fight inflation.
newsitem.headline: Honduras unveils plan to fight inflation.

text.p: Honduran President Carlos Roberto Reina announced a plan to fight inflation that analysts said was aimed at stemming a rising tide of discontent at higher living costs.

In a nationwide address, Reina said the government would promote a $95 million investment project in irrigation, production, warehousing and marketing of basic grains over the next two years to increase supplies and cut prices.

In a bid to put a lid on costs in the so-called basic basket of consumer goods, he also announced plans to bolster the number of low-priced, government-run supermarket outlets and to strengthen consumer protection laws.
Reina, in the last year of a four-year term, has found inflation a stubborn headache while in office.
Honduran inflation was 24.9 percent in 1996, just slightly below the 26.8 percent of 1995. In 1997, the central bank's goal is inflation of 15 percent.
